title: Mysterious Blue-Clad Figure
next_chapter_hook: Su Qingyao's figure vanished at the end of the bamboo grove. Chen Ji clenched his fists, countless questions surging in his heart—how much did she know about his father? And was that turtle shell truly the entirety of the Tianji Record?

text.content: After the crowd dispersed, a cold voice sounded behind Chen Ji: 'Your eyes don't look like those of atrash.' The voice was clear as spring water, yet carried a hint of scrutiny. Chen Ji's heart tightened, but he didn't turn around immediately. He could feel that gaze on his back, carrying the特有的composed of an Inner Sect disciple surveying ants. He calculated rapidly in his mind—why would an Inner Sect disciple appear in the Outer Disciple area? And why specifically target him, this acknowledgedtrash?

dialogue.content: What, not going to turn around and take a look?

text.content: Chen Ji slowly turned around. Before him stood a young woman in blue robes, about seventeen or eighteen years old, with a slender figure and skin like solidified cream. Hanging from her waist was a jade pendant inscribed with the words 'Inner Sect', gleaming warmly in the setting sun. This was a token of status worn only by the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of the Tianqing Sect—Su Qingyao. She gazed at Chen Ji with a smile that wasn't quite a smile, those clear eyes hiding a hint of curiosity, a touch of inquiry, and something else Chen Ji couldn't quite read.

dialogue.content: The Inner Disciple Senior Fellow personally visiting the Outer Sect area—such an honor for Chen Ji. But might I ask what brings the senior sister to see thistrash?

text.content: Su Qingyao let out a light laugh, yet the smile carried no warmth—it was like a cold pool in winter. She took two steps forward, closing the distance between them to within three feet. This proximity made Chen Ji frown slightly—it was too close, close enough to see the curve of her eyelashes, close enough that if she suddenly struck, he would have almost no time to react. But he didn't retreat. Instead, he slightly lowered his gaze, assuming a respectful posture. Only he himself knew that cold sweat had already begun seeping through his back. This woman gave him an extremely dangerous feeling.

Su Qingyao seemed oblivious to his deferential posture, instead circling halfway around him as if examining an interesting object. The setting sun stretched her shadow long, overlapping with Chen Ji's. She suddenly stopped, turning her head to look at him with an oddly meaningful tone: 'I saw everything just now. Everyone was laughing at you, but there was no anger in your eyes—only... calculation.'

dialogue.content: Calculation? The senior sister jokes. Atrash has nothing to calculate, merely counting the days until death.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao seems dissatisfied with your answer. What will you do?

choices.text: Continue feigning ignorance, test her bottom line
choices.description: Maintain thetrash persona, use more exaggerated self-mockery to probe how much she actually knows.
choices.risk_hint: She may have already sensed something amiss; excessive pretense could backfire

text.content: Su Qingyao simply asked that question flatly, yet her tone was like an invisible blade, precisely dissecting the pretense in Chen Ji's words. She didn't press further, instead turning to gaze at the distant horizon. Her voice drifted: 'You know, I investigated a person.' She paused. 'Fifteen years ago, there was someone named Chen Xuan.'

choices.text: Moderately reveal your edge, making her realize you're no simple person
choices.description: Tone down some of thetrash气质, face her with a more composed attitude, letting her know you won't be pushed around.
choices.risk_hint: Premature exposure may invite more trouble

text.content: Su Qingyao's eyes lit up slightly—the predatory gaze disappeared, replaced by a pure, almost appreciative interest. A subtle curve formed at the corner of her lips: 'It seems rumors truly cannot be fully trusted. You're far more interesting than I imagined, Chen Ji.'

choices.text: Reverse the situation, directly inquire about her purpose
choices.description: No longer passively responding, directly question why she came.
choices.visible_cost: Offend the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow
choices.visible_reward: May force her to reveal her true purpose

text.content: Su Qingyao didn't get angry; instead, she laughed lightly. She didn't answer his question, instead producing a jade slip from her sleeve, turning it gently between her fingers: 'Aren't you curious why I came to find you? Why would an Inner Disciple Senior Fellow specifically pay attention to atrash disciple from the Outer Sect?' Her voice carried a hint of seduction. 'Don't you want to know the reason?'

Chen Xuan. These two words exploded like thunder in Chen Ji's mind. His pupils contracted slightly, his fingers tightening involuntarily, his knuckles whitening from the force. But in an instant, he had regained his humble appearance, lowering his eyes to conceal the turbulent emotions churning beneath. Fifteen years. This was the first time in fifteen years someone had spoken his father's name before him. He had to use every ounce of strength to suppress the tempest in his heart, his voice terrifyingly calm: 'Who is Chen Xuan? The senior sister must have the wrong person. Chen Ji is merely an orphan and knows nothing of any Chen Xuan.'

Su Qingyao stressed those two words heavily, as if savoring something amusing. She stepped forward, nearly brushing past Chen Ji, her voice low enough for only the two of them to hear: 'Chen Ji, Servant Disciple of the Tianqing Sect, orphaned, lowest-grade bone structure, still lingering at Qi Refining Third Layer after ten years of cultivation. This is you in the sect archives.' She paused. 'But what I found is different. Fifteen years ago, someone defected from the sect, and his son's whereabouts were unknown. That person's wife died of depression shortly after his defection. And that son... was said to have been taken away, never to be heard from again.'

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao seems to know much about your father. What will you do?

choices.text: Continue denying, but secretly note the extent of what she knows
choices.description: Deny everything, but understand internally that her investigation is quite thorough and you need to reassess her threat level.
choices.visible_cost: May miss opportunity to gain intelligence
choices.risk_hint: She may have more cards yet to reveal

dialogue.content: Your denial is useless. Since I dared to speak it, I naturally have my evidence.

text.content: Su Qingyao stopped, her back to him, her voice carrying an inexplicable quality: 'But don't worry, I didn't come today to expose you. I'm merely... curious.' She turned her head, revealing half of her delicate profile. 'Is that turtle shell you have truly the only thing left by that person fifteen years ago?'

choices.description: Acknowledge knowing some things, but not everything, observe what she actually wants.
choices.risk_hint: Her stance is unclear; this could be a trap

dialogue.content: Senior sister, if you have something to say, perhaps speak directly.

text.content: Su Qingyao turned around, her gaze sharp as a blade, yet when it touched the complex emotions in Chen Ji's eyes, it softened slightly. 'I merely want to tell you,' her voice dropped a few tones, 'when your father left the Tianqing Sect, it wasn't as simple as defection. Some things are far more complicated than you imagine. And some people have been secretly searching for what he left behind.'

Chen Ji's heart was shaken. The Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters sat in the most remote corner of the sect, rarely visited. The setting sun had fully set, and night descended like a massive black veil, shrouding everything in hazy shadows. The wind in the bamboo grove grew cold, carrying the distinctive damp chill of night. He stood there, watching Su Qingyao's retreating figure, his mind a churn of thoughts. Who exactly was this woman? Why would she help him? Or was this itself another trap?

dialogue.content: You don't need to believe me right now. But there's one thing I must warn you—

text.content: Su Qingyao's voice suddenly turned serious, as if stating something extremely important: 'The Sect Founder Ancestor has been investigating some old archives lately, reviewing many documents from fifteen years ago. On the surface, he's purging the sect and整顿宗纪. But I always feel... he has other motives.' She paused. 'Also, you'd better be careful of Han Lie from the Xuanwu Sect. Though he's a martial idiot, he pays格外 close attention to internal affairs of the Tianqing Sect. Lately he's been very close with the Sect Founder Ancestor. I suspect they're plotting something.'

dialogue.content: Why is the senior sister telling me this?

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao has revealed important intelligence. How will you respond?

choices.text: Ask about her true relationship with your father
choices.description: Directly ask why she knows so much about your father, what connection exists between her and your father.
choices.risk_hint: She may be unwilling to disclose

dialogue.content: You're clever, knowing what to ask and what not to ask.

text.content: Su Qingyao smiled faintly, that smile carrying a hint of self-mockery: 'Some things I暂时 cannot tell you. But I can tell you this—your father and I... met once before. That was shortly before he left the Tianqing Sect.' Her gaze grew somewhat distant. 'He entrusted my master with something. My master said that when the time comes, that thing would naturally reach you.'

choices.text: Express willingness to cooperate, exchange for more intelligence
choices.description: Proactively show goodwill, indicate willingness to cooperate,借此换取 more information about your father and the sect.

text.content: Su Qingyao seemed somewhat surprised, one brow arching slightly, genuine surprise flickering in her eyes. Thistrash—in other words, this deeply hidden man—actually took the initiative to propose cooperation? She fell silent for a moment, seemingly reassessing the person before her. After a brief pause, she nodded lightly: 'I can consider it. But before that, I need to see your sincerity.'

Night had fully enveloped the Tianqing Sect, stars slowly twinkling overhead. Su Qingyao's figure appeared cold and distant under the moonlight as she turned to leave. Just as she was about to step into the shadows of the bamboo grove, she suddenly stopped, turned her head, her voice low as if speaking to herself: 'By the way, there's one more thing.' Her voice carried an inexplicable quality. 'What your father left behind... perhaps there was more than just that turtle shell.'

Su Qingyao didn't answer, merely curling her lips into a meaningful smile. Moonlight bathed her face, outlining her silhouette dreamlike and ethereal, yet making the emotions in her eyes difficult to fathom. 'Some things cannot be rushed.' she said softly. 'When it's time for you to know, you naturally will.' With those words, her figure vanished like a wisp of smoke into the depths of the bamboo grove, leaving only a faint fragrance lingering in the air. Chen Ji stood rooted to the spot, night wind ruffling his clothes and bringing waves of cold. He gazed toward where Su Qingyao had disappeared, his eyes dark as ink. This night's encounter had shattered the delicate balance he had meticulously maintained for years. This woman was far more dangerous than he had imagined—not because of her strength, but because she knew too much.

dialogue.content: This girl is no simple person.

text.content: A hoarse voice suddenly rang out in Chen Ji's mind—it was Mo Xiansheng's voice, lingering within the Tianji Record. Chen Ji's heart tightened, but he made no sound, merely standing still. Mo Xiansheng continued: 'She's right. Your father did leave some things behind back then. It's just that those things were hidden in different places—the turtle shell was only one of them.' Chen Ji remained silent, only tightening his fists. Mo Xiansheng's words confirmed his most unwelcome suspicion—his father, fifteen years ago, had been scheming something massive. And these fragments he left behind were now being pieced together bit by bit, willing or not. Was tonight's encounter coincidence, or fate? What was Su Qingyao's true purpose? In the night, Chen Ji turned and walked back to his small hut, his silhouette solitary yet resolute. No matter how many hidden reefs lay ahead, he had to continue— to uncover the truth about his father, and to find his sister who had been missing for years.
